column1: # Each of run A's four state records verified STANDALONE against ONLY its own
# role key. A chain that verifies only as a chain is sequential, not separable,
# and separability is what Success Criterion 4 asks for.
# The verifier here is OpenSSL 3.0.13, not the product. That is deliberate: an
# implementation with no stake in the outcome confirming the same signatures is
# stronger evidence than the product confirming itself. The public key is the
# raw Ed25519 key from the clean-room trust root wrapped in an SPKI header; the
# message is the state's own domain separator followed by the record's body
# The four positive results are paired with TWELVE cross-role controls -- every
# record checked against every OTHER role's key -- and all twelve failed. Without
# those controls, four "Signature Verified Successfully" lines would be equally
# consistent with a verifier that accepts anything.
